utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thierno Souleymane Sow
utterances.text: Vous ne pouvez pas adopter des projets de loi comme l'intro 920 et 1189.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thierno Souleymane Sow
utterances.text: Les appartements, si les travailleurs n'ont nulle part où recharger en toute sécurité, la ville doit développer des bonnes de recharge publique.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thierno Souleymane Sow
utterances.text: Et des armoires d'échange.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thierno Souleymane Sow
utterances.text: des batteries approuvées par le DOT et le FDNY afin d'aider à prévenir les incendies de batteries résidentielles.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thierno Souleymane Sow
utterances.text: Nous avons également besoin de plus de pistes cyclables protégées et de meilleures infrastructures.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thierno Souleymane Sow
utterances.text: Tout dommage que nos vélos subissent dans les rues présente un risque pour la batterie.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thierno Souleymane Sow
utterances.text: Les bornes de recharge constitueraient un premier pas important pour rendre ce travail plus sûr et offrir aux travailleurs le soutien de base dont nous avons besoin.

chapters.summary: Gohim, an Uber delivery worker, says the job involves long hours, dangerous traffic, and no safe place to rest or recharge. Workers have little job security and must charge at home despite knowing the risks. He opposes Intros 920 and 1189 without safe alternatives and calls for public charging hubs, battery swap cabinets, and safer bike infrastructure.

chapters.summary: Corthell, an engineer and former bike mechanic, says e-bike fires can fill a room with toxic smoke in 30 seconds and reach flashpoint in under a minute. She leads a battery safety project using an algorithm developed at Columbia to measure internal electrical precursors to battery failure, has an NSF grant, and is working with FDNY and UL to test an early-warning device.
chapters.title: Lucy Corthell presents early-warning battery safety technology

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Corthell
utterances.text: Hi there, thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Corthell
utterances.text: I'm Lucy Corthell.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Corthell
utterances.text: I'm the oldest daughter raised by a single mom and an engineer and former bike mechanic.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Corthell
utterances.text: Growing up, my mom was always often busy with my brother or at her full-time job, and so I would use a bike to get around everywhere from a young age.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Corthell
utterances.text: I'm not alone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Corthell
utterances.text: It's a fast, clean, and cheap way to get places.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Corthell
utterances.text: So that's why we're here today to talk about the disasters of e-bike battery fires facing every major city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Corthell
utterances.text: This is part of the reason why it's unique is because Underwater Laboratory states it takes only 30 seconds for an e-bike fire to fill a room with toxic smoke.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Corthell
utterances.text: And that's compared to three minutes in a traditional fire.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Corthell
utterances.text: That smoke contains a lot of flammable gases.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Corthell
utterances.text: And so the flash point is only under a minute.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Corthell
utterances.text: So that is when all the gases ignite and it's really hot and dangerous.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Corthell
utterances.text: That is why I'm leading a battery safety project with the mission to protect people and provide an early warning alarm for every home battery.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Corthell
utterances.text: We measure internal electrical precursors to battery failure using a novel algorithm that I helped develop at Columbia University.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Corthell
utterances.text: We also received a National Science Foundation grant for this project, where we attended seven conferences across academia, industry, and nonprofits.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Corthell
utterances.text: What I noticed is that there's a gap between technology and policy that I hope conversations like these can fill.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Corthell
utterances.text: To put people first.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Corthell
utterances.text: For example, in China, they require five minutes of warning before an

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Corthell
utterances.text: electric vehicle fire.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Corthell
utterances.text: And in Europe this spring, they'll implement a battery passport where anyone can scan a QR code on the battery to see what chemistry it is and its state of health.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Corthell
utterances.text: We're working with, my team and I are working with the Fire Department of New York and Underwriter Laboratories to test our early warning device.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Corthell
utterances.text: We would love to build more partnerships, including with local government agencies like NYCHA, who believe in our mission.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Corthell
utterances.text: Ultimately, I hope more technologies like ours can be supported or regulated to put people first.

chapters.summary: Adler, a paramedic with the EMS Public Advocacy Council, says the city thought it was winning fights against building fires and worker exploitation, but battery fires are now a major cause of horrific deaths. He supports fire safety regulation but urges the Council to balance it with protecting immigrant delivery workers' livelihoods and dignity.
chapters.title: Walter Adler supports balancing fire safety and workers' rights

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Walter Adler
utterances.text: My name is Walter Adler.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Walter Adler
utterances.text: I'm a paramedic.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Walter Adler
utterances.text: I'm a representative of the Emergency Medical Services Public Advocacy Council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Walter Adler
utterances.text: There was a time, I think, recently, in our recent memory of this city, when we thought we were winning the war on buildings burning down and killing people alive, and we thought we were winning the war on exploiting immigrant workers,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Walter Adler
utterances.text: and we thought we were winning the war of getting all of our various struggles in this city organized behind the law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Walter Adler
utterances.text: The laws that are being put in place with these intros are wildly important, because as we have seen in the last few years, the majority of the horrific deaths in our city coming from fire are coming from these batteries.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Walter Adler
utterances.text: We have also seen unprecedented exploitation of our Deliverista brothers and sisters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Walter Adler
utterances.text: We have seen how hard it is in a city where so many New Yorkers feel that they are entitled to have food brought to their door pre-cooked, but do not care about 16

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Walter Adler
utterances.text: 24-hour back-breaking shifts of what that entails.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Walter Adler
utterances.text: There is a world where we must regulate fire safety prevention, and EMS PAC supports that world.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Walter Adler
utterances.text: There is a world where we have to protect immigrant workers, and all things need to be in place to protect their livelihoods, their dignity, and their jobs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Walter Adler
utterances.text: And thanks to the Deliveristas,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Walter Adler
utterances.text: and the unions and other forces, we try to put that in place.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Walter Adler
utterances.text: The reason I, as a paramedic, am here to speak today is those horrific fires are where my brothers and sisters have had to show up to care for the wounded and the aftermath of that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Walter Adler
utterances.text: And my brothers and sisters have also shown up when the deliveristas have had their bike wiped out by cars, have gone into cardiac arrest from exhaustion.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Walter Adler
utterances.text: So we urge the council to balance fire safety and workers'rights.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Walter Adler
utterances.text: And we as EMTs and paramedics are always on the side of exploited and oppressed New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Walter Adler
utterances.text: So we say there has to be some balance in what we're regulating.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Walter Adler
utterances.text: And also the opportunities that these laws can provide for our brothers and sister delivery students.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you, Walter.

chapters.summary: Staff thanks Adler and calls the next speaker. Lopez, a paramedic since 2019, says lithium-ion battery fires cause severe burns, smoke inhalation, and respiratory failure, and e-bike collisions also create trauma emergencies. He asks whether the Council is giving EMS infrastructure the same attention as prevention, noting EMS has operated under FDNY without its own commissioner or independent budget for nearly 30 years.
chapters.title: Christian Baer Lopez links battery fires to EMS staffing needs

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Next.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Baer Lopez
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair and members of City Council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Baer Lopez
utterances.text: I'm Christian Bear Lopez, 25, paramedic serving New Yorkers in EMS since 2019.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Baer Lopez
utterances.text: I've testified before this Council about EMS staffing, retention, and response times.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Baer Lopez
utterances.text: Today, I want to connect those concerns to lithium-ion battery safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Baer Lopez
utterances.text: When a lithium-ion battery catches fire, the emergency doesn't end when the flames are extinguished.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Baer Lopez
utterances.text: We're talking about severe burns, smoke inhalation, respiratory failure, and potentially multiple critically injured patients requiring immediate medical attention.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Baer Lopez
utterances.text: But there's another aspect of this conversation we shouldn't overlook.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Baer Lopez
utterances.text: Every day, New Yorkers rely on e-bikes and scooters to travel throughout this city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Baer Lopez
utterances.text: And when those riders are struck by vehicles, we're responding to those emergencies too.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Baer Lopez
utterances.text: We're treating traumatic injuries, head injuries, and patients whose lives can change in seconds.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Baer Lopez
utterances.text: As a paramedic, my concern is what happens when prevention fails, whether that's a battery fire or a collision on our streets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Baer Lopez
utterances.text: Who treats these patients?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Baer Lopez
utterances.text: How quickly can an ambulance arrive?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Baer Lopez
utterances.text: And do we have enough experienced EMTs and paramedics available to respond?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Baer Lopez
utterances.text: These questions matter because our EMS workforce continues to face staffing and retention challenges.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Baer Lopez
utterances.text: For nearly 30 years, EMS has operated under the FDNY without its own commissioner or independent departmental budget.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Baer Lopez
utterances.text: Last week, Councilmember Zuzan Shuang introduced Intro 1182 proposing the independent EMS department.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Baer Lopez
utterances.text: Given the role EMS plays in responding to these emergencies, have members of this council considered sponsoring

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Baer Lopez
utterances.text: during this legislation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Baer Lopez
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting that restructuring EMS will prevent battery fires or traffic collisions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Baer Lopez
utterances.text: I'm asking this council whether we're giving our EMS infrastructure the same attention we're giving prevention.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Baer Lopez
utterances.text: Fire prevention, fire suppression, and emergency medical services are three distinct disciplines, all essential to public safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Baer Lopez
utterances.text: We can work to prevent these emergencies, but we also must be prepared to care for the people who survive them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Baer Lopez
utterances.text: Thank you, and with that, I yield my time.

chapters.summary: Sanchez thanks Lopez and calls the next speaker. Mahamat, an Uber Eats and DoorDash worker, says e-bikes are their livelihood and batteries are essential. Because there are too few public charging options, workers bring batteries home, endangering themselves, families, neighbors, and buildings. He opposes Intro 920 without safe alternatives and calls for public charging and battery swap infrastructure.

chapters.summary: Ariola moves to virtual testimony and calls Regis Doucette. Doucette says lithium-ion batteries are in many devices beyond e-bikes and pose persistent life-safety risks. He describes thermal runaway producing hydrogen fluoride and hydrogen cyanide, which can penetrate protective gear and transfer contamination, and says some extinguishers with UL components can address lithium-ion fires.
chapters.title: Regis Doucette warns of toxic gases and persistent lithium-ion hazards

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: Okay, we will now turn to the virtual panelists.

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: For virtual panelists, once your name is called, a member of our staff will unmute you, and the sergeant at arms will set up.

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: the timer and give you the go ahead to begin.

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: Please wait for the sergeant to announce that you may begin before delivering your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: I will now call our first panel of virtual

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: Virtual testimony, Regis Doucette.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: Time starts.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: You are, we cannot hear you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: Okay, sorry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: Thank you, Chairs Areola and Sanchez, and of course, Council Speaker Bannon, and a special prayer to Aunt Wendy for her awful travail.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: The widespread use of lithium ion batteries introduces significant new life safety risks and specific hazards, home and office specific, not just e-bikes,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: vapes, portable computers, cell phones, flashlights, tools, razors, wheelchairs, even UPS systems.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: They're all embedded inside a device.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: They're not stored inside a cabinet like a spare tire.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: They deserve a red tag, meaning what New York State's program is all about.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: And you'll see why in a few moments.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: Many structure fires will have the lithium-ion battery presence inside it, so this is not an occasional but a persistent threat to our firefighters and first responders and the dwellers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: So, when a battery management system fails and triggers thermal runaway, it produces toxic gases such as hydrogen fluoride and hydrogen cyanide.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: Hydrogen fluoride acts as a severe corrosive to the eyes, the skin, and digestive system, which, with body moisture, turns into an acid.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: Hydrogen cyanide deprives cells of oxygen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: Both gases interfere tremendously with our systems.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: So these contaminants can penetrate up to three layers of protective gear on the firemen, and they're exceptionally difficult to decontaminate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: Symptoms of the exposure for the humans can take up to two or three hours to feel.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: These are non-visible hazards and they are easily transferred via the gear, the tools, the personal items.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: It's awful.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: The takeaway is, well, the takeaway, they transfer out of a site and that's an awful situation for us citizens.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: Now, for a prior suppression solution that actually suppresses those toxic gases.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: Finally, it is true that lithium-ion batteries do not get extinguished by current fire extinguishers, which in fact can worsen the situation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: There are extinguishers out there that have UL registered components for A and B fires and put out lithium ion fires also.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: Time has expired.

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: Do you want to just wrap up?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: You're so gracious.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: So, and you can actually get them right now, and I'll send the information to the team.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: One last quick cheerleader thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: New York has always been innovative in fire suppression by fighting fires inside buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: So a new day, a new challenge, New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Regis Doucette
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Ariola thanks Doucette and calls Philip Handel M. Thomas. Thomas offers condolences to fire victims and thanks FDNY, EMS, and NYPD. He says his company has analyzed over 10,000 global battery situations and is developing safety intelligence within batteries to detect precursors and suppress thermal runaway. He recommends enforcing Local Law 39 and restoring e-bike trade-in funding.
chapters.title: Philip Handel M. Thomas recommends battery safety intelligence and trade-in funding

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Philip Handel M. Thomas

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Philip Handel M. Thomas
utterances.text: But I'd like to point out very quickly a few recommendations, which is the safety enforcement of local law 39 of 2023.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Philip Handel M. Thomas
utterances.text: I would like to also recommend the restoration on funds and the fund, the e-bike trade-in program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Philip Handel M. Thomas

summary: Committee on Fire and Emergency Management and Housing and Buildings held a joint oversight hearing on residential fires and lithium-ion battery dangers, with seven related bills.
FDNY Commissioner Bonsignore and First Deputy Commissioner Flynn testified on fire fatalities, battery fire trends, enforcement, and legislation; HPD and DOB also answered questions.

Public testimony included firefighters, delivery workers, safety technology companies, and families of victims, with repeated calls for safe outdoor charging, trade-in programs, and stronger enforcement.
title: Committee on Fire and Emergency Management
topic: Oversight - Residential Fires and the Dangers of Lithium-Ion Batteries
